title: A timed-out receiver can still acquire a file descriptor after cleanup
applies_when: A caller joins a background fd receiver with a timeout, then raises or cleans a shared descriptor collection while the receiver can still return from recvmsg. Also inspect sender exceptions and partial receive failures before ownership is returned to the caller.
lesson: A join timeout is not worker cancellation. Trace the ownership handoff, including resources received after the failed call returns. In SGLang exchange_posix_fds, serialize descriptor insertion and failure cleanup with the same lock; record failed ownership before closing accumulated descriptors, and close a late incoming descriptor instead of publishing it. Transfer ownership only on success. Test with real UNIX sockets and SCM_RIGHTS: pause the second receive, let the caller time out, then release the peer and receiver. Assert both accumulated and late descriptors are invalid, outgoing caller-owned descriptors remain valid, and success still returns live descriptors. A fake completed thread or a snapshot-only fd count cannot establish that late arrivals are cleaned.
avoid_when: Do not close caller-owned successful results or resources whose ownership was never transferred. This does not prove that a daemon receiver has stopped, interrupt accept/recvmsg, repair malformed ancillary-message parsing, or qualify CUDA mappings, multi-process collectives, model correctness or inference speed. Different socket backends and worker lifetime policies need their own tests. The linked PR is contributor-tested, not evidence of maintainer acceptance or improved Scout discovery accuracy.

evidence.note: Pinned repair serializes late fd insertion with unsuccessful-exit cleanup and preserves successful caller ownership. This changes descriptor lifetime, not the existing socket timeout or daemon-thread policy.

Six contributor-run Linux CPU cases use real SCM_RIGHTS and fstat with injected rendezvous/failure/late-receive barriers: four unchanged-main regression cases fail, six patched cases pass. A separate 20-repeat late-receive stress preserves process fd count. No GPU, multi-process Gloo or full official dependency qualification is claimed.
